estadio-afonso-henriques.name: Estádio D. Afonso Henriques
estadio-afonso-henriques.short: Home ground of Vitória SC in Guimarães: opened in 1965 and rebuilt for Euro 2004 with 30,029 seats
estadio-afonso-henriques.long: The Estádio D. Afonso Henriques is the home ground of Vitória Sport Clube in Guimarães. The first stadium, built to a design by the architect Mário Bonito, opened on 3 January 1965; in the inaugural match Vitória beat Belenenses 2–1. The ground was first expanded for the 1991 FIFA World Youth Championship, and on 30 September 1995 the members chose the name D. Afonso Henriques. For Euro 2004 it was completely rebuilt in 2002–2003: capacity rose to 30,029 and the seats were laid out in medieval patterns. It hosted the Euro 2004 matches Denmark–Italy and Italy–Bulgaria.
estadio-afonso-henriques.history:
Before this stadium, Vitória played at the grounds of Amorosa, Atouguia, José Minotes, Perdiz and Benlhevai. In 1962 a competition was announced for a new stand, and the Portuguese Football Federation then required every first-division club to play on grass. On 3 January 1965, though the work was not yet finished, the Municipal Stadium of Guimarães was formally opened, designed by the architect Mário Bonito. It held about 15,000 spectators and cost some 8,500 contos. In the first match Vitória beat Belenenses 2–1; in the 9th minute Albertino Castro, a product of the club's own youth ranks, scored the first goal at the new ground, and Inácio scored the winner late on.

On 27 December 1989 the municipal assembly voted to hand the stadium to the club, and a deed of 21 September 1990 completed the sale to Vitória for one million escudos. For the 1991 FIFA World Youth Championship, hosted by Portugal, the ground had its first major remodelling: the north stand was built and part of the east stand enlarged.

On 30 September 1995 a general meeting of the club decided the stadium's name. The options included "Afonso Henriques", "Vitória Sport Clube" and the discarded "Amorosa" and "José Maria Castro Rodrigues". By 453 votes to 358 the members chose D. Afonso Henriques, in honour of the first King of Portugal, who was born in Guimarães.

In 1998 Guimarães was chosen as one of the host cities of Euro 2004, and the municipality and the club signed a sports development agreement. Between 11 March 2002 and 25 July 2003 the stadium underwent a deep reconstruction that made it one of the finest football grounds in the country. The design was by a local architect, Eduardo Guimarães: with a new south stand he closed the bowl, so that from the street it looks like an ordinary building, while green areas and good access were added around it. The municipality bore the whole cost — about 34 million euros; it was the cheapest of the ten Euro 2004 venues and the only one with no cost overrun. The arrangement of the seats recalls a medieval tournament: D. Afonso Henriques is picked out on the south upper tier, and coloured flags on the others. The tiles in the bars and toilets are decorated with the castle of Guimarães, shields, helmets and swords.

On 25 July 2003 the rebuilt ground was formally handed to Vitória under the name Estádio D. Afonso Henriques. About 29,865 people watched a multimedia show and a match against 1. FC Kaiserslautern, which the home side won 4–1; the scorers were Afonso Martins (who opened the scoring at the new ground), Nuno Assis, Rubens Júnior and Guga. At Euro 2004 the stadium hosted two Group C matches: on 14 June Denmark and Italy drew 0–0 before 29,595 spectators, and on 22 June Italy beat Bulgaria 2–1.

In 2015 the stadium marked its 50th anniversary. In 2019 it hosted two matches of the first UEFA Nations League, after which the municipality granted the club €88,500 to replace structures on the west and north stand façades and install two large screens. In 2021 Vitória began a phased replacement of the seats with tip-up models and the creation of an away-fan security box.
facts: The stadium opened on 3 January 1965 as the Municipal Stadium of Guimarães; the first match was Vitória 2–1 Belenenses.
On 30 September 1995 the club's members chose the name D. Afonso Henriques by 453 votes to 358.
The Euro 2004 rebuild ran from 11 March 2002 to 25 July 2003 and cost about 34 million euros.
Capacity is 30,029; it was the cheapest of the ten Euro 2004 venues and the only one with no cost overrun.
At Euro 2004 it hosted Denmark–Italy (0–0) and Italy–Bulgaria (2–1).
estadio-afonso-henriques.tip: The stadium stands in the middle of the city, about a 15-minute walk from the historic centre. Vitória's matches follow the fixture list; outside match days you cannot go in, but the tiled façades and the statue of Afonso Henriques by the entrance can be seen at any time. Stadium tours are arranged on request through the club. It pairs easily with the castle and the Palace of the Dukes of Braganza, ten minutes away on foot.
